subject: Post-call: AcmeHealth Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Private VPC data flow & next steps

Hi Jamie — great to speak earlier. Thanks for walking us through AcmeHealth's requirements. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of requirements we noted:
- Private/VPC deployment preferred (VPC peering or PrivateLink).
- PII: patient identifiers will be sent to the model; cannot leave US region.
- Data retention: logs/inputs should be retained for 90 days max; redaction preferred where possible.
- Logging & audit: need detailed request/response audit logs and token-level usage for billing reconciliation.
- Egress controls: no outbound traffic allowed except to whitelisted Redwood endpoints; on-prem/air-gapped option may be required for some workloads.

Next steps we propose:
1) I will share a VPC dataflow diagram and our private deployment security brief (attached) for your security team to review.
2) Schedule a focused dataflow review with your security/architecture folks and our security lead (Neha). Can you confirm availability next week?
3) Please list any strict non-starters (e.g., cannot use KMS in cloud, full air-gap required, etc.) so we can scope the on-prem options.

Attached: vpc-dataflow-diagram.png, redwood-private-deployment-security-brief.pdf

If that looks right, I’ll loop in Neha and Rishi and propose a few times.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Private VPC data flow & next steps

Thanks Marissa — solid summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Data residency: All PHI must remain in the US region. No processing in multi-region configurations.
- PII handling: We will need the ability to redact or pseudonymize direct identifiers before they reach any third-party model if feasible.
- Retention: 90 days for raw inputs is acceptable; audit logs may be retained longer on a case-by-case basis but must be accessible to us.
- Logging: We need request ID correlation between our logs and Redwood logs for debugging.
- On-prem/air-gap: Certain clinical workloads will require an on-prem appliance with zero egress. For the initial PoC, we can start with VPC-only deployment but may scope an air-gapped option later.

I'm looping our solution architect (Oliver) separately, but for scheduling let's aim for next Tue/Wed morning Pacific. Please include your security lead.

Best,
Jamie Liu
Head of Infrastructure | AcmeHealth
jamie.liu@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Private VPC data flow & next steps

Thanks Jamie — appreciate the clarity. Looping in Neha (Security) and Rishi (Solutions) to coordinate the dataflow review. Attached is the VPC dataflow diagram and a short security brief that maps to your bullets.

Proposed times for a 60-minute dataflow + controls session:
- Tue, 21 Apr, 9:00–10:00 PT
- Tue, 21 Apr, 11:00–12:00 PT
- Wed, 22 Apr, 10:00–11:00 PT

Neha / Rishi — can you confirm which slot works and whether you need any additional artifacts (network ACLs, KMS/HSM details, SOC2 artifacts)?

Notes on our side: 
- VPC options: we support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink. For strict egress controls we can deploy within your VPC with no routing to the public internet; all telemetry can be pushed to an account you control.
- KMS: We support customer-managed KMS keys in your account for data at rest; HSM-backed keys can be discussed for on-prem appliances.
- Logs: We can provide structured audit logs with request IDs; we also support streaming logs to your logging bucket (S3) or SIEM via PrivateLink.

Attachment: vpc-dataflow-diagram.png (image/png) — please review the arrows labeled "egress gateway" and "redwood control plane"; we can suppress control plane egress in private deployments where required.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Private VPC data flow & next steps

Thanks for the context — a few items from security for the dataflow call: 

Checklist / questions for the session:
- Confirm whether customer-managed KMS in AcmeHealth account is acceptable (preferred). If not, provide justification for lack of CMK.
- Clarify which artifacts Acme needs: SOC2 Type II report, network ACLs, architecture diagrams, config examples for PrivateLink/VPC peering.
- Egress: we need a definitive list of allowed destinations. If zero-egress is required for some workloads, we'll scope an on-prem/air-gapped appliance.
- Logging: confirm retention window for audit logs; Redwood can optionally redact PII from logs before delivery, but we need a signed agreement on what gets redacted.
- Data flows: for pseudonymization patterns, we will propose a preprocessing hook to run inside your VPC before data is sent to the model.

Please have Jamie/Oliver confirm the acceptable artifacts and the expected retention for audit logs. Marissa — once they confirm, we’ll prepare the technical runbook and an example CloudFormation snippet for PrivateLink.

-Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Private VPC data flow & next steps

Thanks everyone — Tue 21 Apr 11:00–12:00 PT works for us. A couple quick answers ahead of the call:

- CMK: We prefer customer-managed KMS keys in our account for the PoC.
- Artifacts: SOC2 Type II is required; the dataflow diagram you sent is helpful. Please bring PrivateLink and VPC peering config examples.
- Retention: 90 days raw inputs; audit logs can be retained up to 1 year but must be exportable.
- On-prem: For the initial PoC we’ll start VPC-only. We will evaluate an air-gapped appliance for clinical workloads in phase 2.

Looking forward to the call — Jamie
